review_notes: I read the whole target file (83 lines) and checked every proof against the declarations it invokes. `gradedIdempotentHeadBasis` (lines 45-60) is a direct application of `TauCeti.gradedSimpleClassBasis` (`TauCeti/Algebra/Category/GradedModuleCat/CartanMap/SimpleBasis.lean:171-174`), which takes exactly the three data `hne`, `hself`, `hS` supplied here; the two anonymous arguments are one-line appeals to `smulGradedDimension_gradedIdempotentHead` (`TauCeti/Algebra/Category/GradedModuleCat/Idempotent/Head.lean:386-388`, conclusion `= if j = i then 1 else 0`), closed respectively by `simp` with `j ≠ i` and by `simp` at `j = i`. The `classical` calls in each block are genuinely required because that lemma carries a `[DecidableEq I]` binder and the enclosing `def` has no decidable equality instance, so they cannot simply be dropped. The two wrapper theorems (lines 62-79) are one-step applications of `gradedSimpleClassBasis_apply` (SimpleBasis.lean:178-181) and `gradedSimpleClassBasis_repr_apply` (SimpleBasis.lean:186-198); `Module.Basis.mk_apply` in Mathlib (`Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Basis/Basic.lean:122-123`) is not a definitional equality, so no `rfl`-style collapse of these wrappers is available, and the statements deliberately spell out `⟨gradedPositiveMulQuotient …⟩` rather than the private abbrev `headFamily` so that the `[simp]` lemmas are usable downstream (cf. uses in `CartanMap/ExtEuler/Matrix.lean:183` and `CartanMap/ExtEuler/Poincare.lean:109-110`). I considered and rejected as mere style (not proof simplification) the following: hoisting the two `classical` calls into a single `classical` at the top of a `by` block; eta-reducing `fun i => headFamily he₀ i`; dropping `by exact` from the two wrapper proofs; inlining the single-use `headFamily` abbrev. None of these removes a redundant mathematical step or makes a key idea easier to follow, so no finding is reported. Limitation: I could not elaborate any candidate replacement, so all observations are based on reading source only.
